name: My submission history
description: The session check could not be a join inside the aggregate, as it is on the other authed reads: json_agg with no GROUP BY returns exactly one row whatever it is fed, so a revoked session would have got 200 with an empty list -- a rejection indistinguishable from having submitted nothing. The aggregate is therefore a scalar subquery and live_sessions is the outer FROM, which yields no row at all when the session is dead. A live session with no submissions still yields one row holding '[]'. The row is what distinguishes the two cases, so `deny` tests the `session_ok` marker projected from live_sessions rather than `body`: an empty list is falsy to the condition evaluator, and testing `body` would have rejected every user who has not submitted yet. It runs first and is terminal: a condition-gated terminal task is how a workflow refuses a request while choosing its own status code, which has to be 401 here. Postgres builds the response: the `body` column is json_agg, and since Orion 1.6 a json column decodes as the document itself, so the respond task copies it into data.body.

input.query: SELECT (SELECT coalesce(json_agg(x ORDER BY x.created_at DESC), '[]'::json) FROM ( SELECT m.id, u.handle AS owner, g.slug AS game, m.version, m.repo, m.release_tag,        m.weight_class AS class, m.size_bytes, m.status, m.reject_reason, m.created_at FROM models m JOIN users u ON u.id = m.owner_id JOIN games g ON g.id = m.game_id WHERE m.owner_id = ($1)::uuid   AND (($2)::text IS NULL OR g.slug = ($2)::text)) x) AS body, ls.sid AS session_ok FROM live_sessions ls WHERE ls.sid = ($3)::uuid AND ls.user_id = ($1)::uuid
